decisionBoard.title: Most business owners who come to me are in one of these situations.
decisionBoard.summary: Either you don't have a website and nothing solid to send an interested customer, or you have one that no longer reflects the business you run today. Either way, the first step is the same: work out what your customer needs to hear before they get in touch.
decisionBoard.label: Is this you?

process.label: How it works
title: From your first message
to a live website.
process.text: Four simple steps. You always know what's happening, and we don't move forward until you've approved each stage.
process.ctaText: Want to know what this could look like for your business?

items.title: A quick chat
items.text: You tell me, in plain language, what the business does, who your customers are and what you want people to do when they visit the site. From that, I work out what the site needs to say and in what order.

items.title: I write the copy
items.text: I take what you've told me, organise it and write all the copy for the site. You read it, make any corrections and approve it.

items.title: Custom design
items.text: Once the copy is approved, I design the site around it. No off-the-shelf template — a design that actually feels like your business.

items.title: Build and launch
items.text: I build the site, test it on phones and computers, and put it live. You get a finished website that works properly.

about.label: Who's behind it
about.title: I'm Pini. I handle everything myself.
paragraphs: I work on every site myself, from the first conversation and the copy and design all the way through to launch.
When the same person listens, writes and designs, nothing gets lost along the way. You don't have to explain the same thing three times to three different people.

strengths.title: One person from start to finish

strengths.title: Design that fits your business

strengths.title: A clear price upfront

faq.label: FAQ
faq.title: Questions people usually ask
faq.text: The things business owners tend to ask before making a decision.
faq.contactText: Got a question that isn't here?

items.question: What kind of website does my business need?
items.answer: A landing page is best when you're promoting one service or offer. A one-page website works when everything a customer needs to know can fit comfortably on one page. A full website makes sense when you offer several different services and each one needs its own explanation. I'll help you choose the right option for your business.

items.question: How much does a small-business website cost?
items.answer: Landing pages start at ₪2,900, one-page websites at ₪3,900 and full websites at ₪6,900. The final price depends on the size and complexity, and includes learning about your business, writing the copy, design, development and mobile optimisation. You'll get the full scope and final price before we begin.

items.question: How long does it take?
items.answer: Around one week for a landing page, about 10 days for a one-page website and up to three weeks for a full website. The clock starts after the first payment and doesn't include time spent waiting for your feedback.

items.question: Will my website show up on Google?
items.answer: Yes. Every site I build launches with the basics Google needs: a clear structure, copy based on what your customers actually search for, fast loading, mobile optimisation and Google indexing. To be clear, appearing on Google isn't the same as ranking first. Reaching the top in a competitive field usually takes ongoing SEO, which is a separate service. What I do promise is a website built on the right foundation from day one.

items.question: Do I need to bring finished copy or content?
items.answer: No. I write all the copy. If you already have useful material, we'll use it as a starting point. You just need to tell me about the business and approve what I write.

items.question: How many rounds of changes are included?
items.answer: We review the copy and design, make the agreed changes and only move forward once you've approved each stage. The exact number of revision rounds depends on the project and is written clearly in the proposal before we begin.

items.question: What if I don't like the result?
items.answer: That rarely happens because nothing moves forward without your approval. You review the copy before the design begins, and approve the design before I build the site. If something doesn't feel right, we talk about it, fix it and only then move on. There shouldn't be any surprise at the end.

items.question: What happens after the website goes live?
items.answer: You can still come to me for small updates and ongoing maintenance after launch.

finalCta.title: Want to talk about your website?
finalCta.text: Send me a quick message with what your business does and what's missing. I'll come back with a straight answer: what I recommend, what it costs and how long it takes. And if a website isn't what your business needs right now, I'll tell you that too.

nichePages.metaTitle: Websites for Beauty and Skincare Clinics | NorthSpark Studio
nichePages.metaDescription: A website for your beauty clinic or skincare business, with clear treatment pages, easy booking and a design that builds trust. Copy, design and development by one person.
nichePages.eyebrow: Websites for beauty and skincare businesses
nichePages.title: Your clinic's website should start selling before a customer even calls
nichePages.intro: Most beauty clients decide where to book before they ever pick up the phone. They check Instagram, Google the business and look for a reason to trust it. A good website gives them one: it explains each treatment, shows the real clinic and makes booking simple.

painPoints.title: Every treatment needs its own explanation
painPoints.text: Someone choosing between treatments wants to know what's involved, how long it takes and whether it's right for them. An Instagram photo can't answer all that.

painPoints.title: Booking should be easy
painPoints.text: No hunting for a phone number between posts. A clear WhatsApp or call button is always within reach.

painPoints.title: Build trust before they arrive
painPoints.text: Real photos and a clear introduction to the clinic and the person behind it turn a curious visitor into someone ready to book.

nichePages.whatsappMessage: Hi, I'm interested in a website for a beauty clinic
nichePages.relatedLinkLabel: I also build websites for beauty clinics

sections.title: What's included in a beauty clinic website
paragraphs: A website for a beauty clinic, skincare studio or beautician should do what Instagram can't: explain each treatment clearly, introduce the clinic and the person behind it, and make booking easy.
I write, design and build the site myself. There's no need to coordinate between a copywriter, a designer and a developer, and every decision stays in one place.
bullets: A clear explanation of each treatment: what's involved, how long it takes and who it's right for.
A section introducing the clinic and the practitioner, with real photos.
A prominent WhatsApp or call button for booking, within reach on every screen.
A custom design that reflects the feel of your clinic, not a template that looks like everyone else's.
A clear structure that works well on phones and that Google understands, so people searching for your name find organised information.

sections.title: Why it matters for beauty clinics
paragraphs: Most clients decide where to book before they ever get in touch. They check Instagram, Google the business and look for a reason to trust it. When the information is scattered across posts and stories, it's hard to tell exactly what you're getting.
A good website answers the questions you hear again and again, so the people who contact you already know what they want. That saves you time in messages and gives clients the confidence to book.

sections.title: How it works
paragraphs: Four simple steps, and you always know what's happening. We don't move forward until you approve.
bullets: A quick chat: you tell me about the clinic, your treatments and the clients you want more of.
Copy: I write everything on the site, including an explanation of each treatment. You read it, correct it and approve it.
Design: once the copy is approved, I design the site around it in a style that fits your clinic.
Build and launch: I build it, test it on phones and computers, and put it live. You get a finished website that works.

sections.title: How pricing works
paragraphs: The price depends on the scope. For most clinics, a one-page website that brings together your treatments, the clinic and how to get in touch is the right fit. If you offer many treatments that each need their own page, a full website may suit you better.

The prices on the site are starting points. After a short chat you get a clear proposal with the final price before we begin, and payment is split into three parts: 50% upfront, 30% when the design is approved and 20% before launch. Once the site is live, you can still come to me for small updates and maintenance.

faq.question: I already have an active Instagram. Why do I need a website?
faq.answer: Instagram is great for showing your work, but it's hard to explain each treatment properly there. A website brings everything together in one place and leads straight to booking, and you can link to it from your bio.

faq.question: Who writes the treatment descriptions?
faq.answer: I do. Based on a conversation with you, I write all the copy, and you read, correct and approve it before we move on to design.

faq.question: Can clients book through the website?
faq.answer: The site leads to booking through a prominent WhatsApp or call button on every screen. If you already use a booking system, the site can link to it.

faq.question: How long does it take?
faq.answer: It depends on the scope. A one-page website is usually ready in about 10 days, and a full website in up to three weeks, once the materials are in place.

faq.question: What if I add new treatments later?
faq.answer: You can come to me after launch for small updates and maintenance, such as adding a new treatment.

nichePages.metaTitle: Websites for Plumbers, Electricians and Tradespeople | NorthSpark Studio
nichePages.metaDescription: Websites for plumbers, electricians and tradespeople, with real work, quick contact and trust before the first call. Copy, design and development by one person.
nichePages.title: When customers need a tradesperson, they're usually checking a few at once
nichePages.intro: Someone looking for a plumber, electrician or contractor will often contact several people at the same time. The first one to respond with something professional and trustworthy has a real advantage. A website that shows your work and makes it easy to call can be what wins the job.

painPoints.title: You're not the only person they're checking
painPoints.text: A website with real work and solid proof can help you win the job before a competitor even answers the phone.

painPoints.title: People need to see your work
painPoints.text: Show them jobs you've actually completed, not just word-of-mouth recommendations. People want to see before they trust.

painPoints.title: Make it easy to call from a phone
painPoints.text: A clear call or WhatsApp button, with no forms and no searching for your number.

nichePages.whatsappMessage: Hi, I'm interested in a website for my trade business
nichePages.relatedLinkLabel: I also build websites for tradespeople

sections.title: What's included in a website for tradespeople
paragraphs: A website for an electrician, plumber, contractor or any other tradesperson has one main job: help someone who needs help right now see that you're the right person, and get them to call. That's why every site I build for tradespeople starts with the questions your customers are already asking, not with a template.
I write, design and build the whole site myself, from start to finish. You don't need to write copy, find a designer or coordinate between several people.
bullets: All the copy written for you: what you do, where you work, which jobs you take on and why people should choose you.
A gallery of jobs you've completed, with a short note on each one, so people can see your work rather than just hear about it.
Clear call and WhatsApp buttons, available from every screen, with no awkward forms.
A custom design that looks like your business and works properly on phones, where most customers search.
A structure Google understands: clear headings, service descriptions and the basic information that helps you show up in search.

sections.title: Why it matters for tradespeople
paragraphs: When something breaks at home, people don't wait. They search, contact a few tradespeople at once and go with whoever looks most professional and trustworthy. Word of mouth still works, but even someone who got your number from a friend will usually look you up before calling.
A clear website with real work and an easy way to get in touch helps you be the one they call first. It answers common questions in advance, so the first conversation already starts with trust.

sections.title: How it works
paragraphs: The process is simple, and you always know what's happening. We don't move to the next step until you approve.
bullets: A quick chat: you tell me in plain language what you do, who your customers are and which jobs you want more of.
Copy: I organise what you told me and write everything that goes on the site. You read it, correct it and approve it.
Design: once the copy is approved, I design the site around it, including a proper place for photos of your work.
Build and launch: I build it, test it on phones and computers, and put it live. You get a finished website that works.

sections.title: How pricing works
paragraphs: The price depends on the scope. For most tradespeople, a one-page website that brings everything a customer needs into one place is the right fit. If you offer several different kinds of work that each need their own explanation, a full website with a page for each service may suit you better.

The prices on the site are starting points. After a short chat you get a clear proposal with the final price before we begin, and payment is split into three parts: 50% upfront, 30% when the design is approved and 20% before launch. Once the site is live, you can still come to me for small updates and maintenance.

faq.question: I don't have time to write copy. Is that a problem?
faq.answer: No. I write all the copy myself based on a short conversation with you. You just read it, make any corrections and approve it.

faq.question: I don't have many photos of my work. Can we still do this?
faq.answer: Yes. We can start with the photos you have and add more over time. A few real photos with a short explanation are better than a generic gallery.

faq.question: Will the site work well on phones?
faq.answer: Yes. Most people looking for a tradesperson search on their phone, so I test every site on phones and computers before launch, with call and WhatsApp buttons available from every screen.

faq.question: How long does it take?
faq.answer: It depends on the scope. A one-page website is usually ready in about 10 days, and a full website in up to three weeks, once the materials are in place.

faq.question: What happens after the site goes live?
faq.answer: The site is yours, and you can still come to me for small updates and maintenance, for example when you want to add new jobs to the gallery.

nichePages.metaTitle: Donation Pages for Nonprofits | NorthSpark Studio
nichePages.metaDescription: A nonprofit donation page that explains why the work matters and lets people donate without leaving the page. Copy, design and development by one person.
nichePages.title: Once someone decides to donate, every extra step makes them less likely to finish
nichePages.intro: A good donation page doesn't send people somewhere else or leave them with unanswered questions. It quickly explains where the money goes and why it matters, then lets them donate right there on the page.

painPoints.title: Donating should be simple
painPoints.text: Let people donate on the same page, without jumping between screens or filling out a long, awkward form.

painPoints.title: People give when they understand why
painPoints.text: Explain clearly where the money goes and why it matters. A donation button on its own isn't enough.

painPoints.title: Trust is everything
painPoints.text: Real photos and honest information matter. A generic-looking page can make a potential donor hesitate.

nichePages.whatsappMessage: Hi, I'm interested in a donation page for a nonprofit
nichePages.relatedLinkLabel: I also build donation pages for nonprofits

sections.title: What's included in a nonprofit donation page
paragraphs: A good donation page needs to do two things: briefly explain where the money goes and why it matters, and let people donate right away on the same screen. Every extra step, every jump to another page and every awkward form makes it less likely that a donor will finish.
I write, design and build the page myself, so the message, the design and the technical experience are created together and serve one goal.
bullets: Short, clear copy: what the organisation does, who the donation helps and why now.
A way to donate on the same page, without sending donors somewhere else.
Real photos and transparent information that build trust.
A custom design that feels trustworthy rather than generic, and works well on phones.
A clear structure Google understands, so people searching for the organisation find organised information.

sections.title: Why it matters for nonprofits
paragraphs: People give when they understand why. A donation button on its own isn't enough, and a generic-looking page can make a potential donor hesitate. Someone arriving from a WhatsApp link or a social post needs to understand within seconds what you're asking and why it matters.
A focused page that explains, shows and lets people donate straight away removes friction at the moment someone has already decided to help.

sections.title: How it works
paragraphs: Four simple steps. You always know what's happening, and we don't move forward without your approval.
bullets: A quick chat: you tell me about the organisation, its work and what you want donors to do.
Copy: I write everything on the page. You read it, correct it and approve it.
Design: once the copy is approved, I design the page around it.
Build and launch: I build it, test it on phones and computers, and put it live. You get a finished page that works.

sections.title: What to prepare and what you get
paragraphs: You don't need ready-made copy or a detailed plan. A short chat is enough: tell me what the organisation does, who it helps and what you want people to do when they land on the page. I organise and write everything else.

What really helps is real material from your work: photos of your activity, your volunteers and the people you help, plus details about what a donation makes possible. Real photos and honest information build far more trust than a generic design, so it's worth gathering them in advance.

At the end you get a finished donation page that works on phones and computers, with a clear message and a way to donate on the same screen. You can share the link on WhatsApp, post it on social media or link to it from your existing website, and once it's live you can still come to me for small updates, for example before your next campaign.

sections.title: How pricing works
paragraphs: The price depends on the scope. For most nonprofits, a focused landing page with one message and one action, to donate, is the right fit. If you also want to present your wider activity, a one-page website or a full website may suit you better.

The prices on the site are starting points. After a short chat you get a clear proposal with the final price before we begin, and payment is split into three parts: 50% upfront, 30% when the design is approved and 20% before launch. Once the page is live, you can still come to me for small updates and maintenance.

faq.question: Can people donate directly from the page?
faq.answer: Yes, that's the point. The page is built so donors can give on the same screen without moving between pages. The payment setup is matched to what your organisation already uses.

faq.question: Who writes the copy?
faq.answer: I do. Based on a short conversation, I write all the copy, and you read, correct and approve it.

faq.question: We already have a website. Do we need a new one?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. A focused donation page can stand on its own and be linked from your existing site, campaigns and social channels.

faq.question: How long does it take?
faq.answer: A focused landing page is usually ready in about a week, once the materials are in place.

faq.question: Can the page be updated for the next campaign?
faq.answer: Yes. Once the page is live, you can still come to me for small updates and maintenance.
